- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling sharply.
- Model frequently overshoots after a strong upward move (e.g., +5+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was positive; apply a “cool-down” correction by subtracting 1–3% from peak forecast.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70–72), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day of divergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be overly optimistic in early days (e.g., first 5–7 days) when sentiment is positive; dampen initial forecast by 1–2%.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-period, model often fails to adjust; check for sudden drop in sentiment and reduce forecast by 1–3% per day of negative sentiment.
- When true outcome is below 65 and model is above 70, model is overconfident; apply downward bias of 5–10% if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment is mixed (±0.33) and price is volatile, model often overfits short-term noise; use 3-day moving average to smooth forecast.
